options.B: To stop mothers from bringing their babies for future visits
options.C: To investigate vaccine safety and maintain public trust in the program
options.D: To immediately ban all vaccine manufacturing in the country

explanation: Exactly right! Reporting helps health teams track safety, catch batch issues early, and keep parents confident in immunizations.

question: Why is it so important to help a mother keep her bladder empty during prolonged labour?

options.A: It lowers the mother's blood pressure instantly
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from producing urine altogether
options.C: It stops the uterus from contracting spontaneously
options.D: A full bladder can obstruct fetal descent and slow labour

explanation: Think of the pelvic space as crowded! A full bladder gets in the way, making it harder for the baby's head to move down naturally.

question: How can a nurse tell the difference between a cerebellar intention tremor and a Parkinsonian resting tremor?

options.A: The parkinsonian tremor worsens when reaching for a cup of coffee
options.B: The parkinsonian tremor disappears with rapid alternating movements
options.C: The cerebellar tremor becomes more pronounced as the patient approaches a target
options.D: The cerebellar tremor only appears when the patient is completely asleep

explanation: An intention tremor acts up right as your hand gets close to what it's trying to grab (like reaching for a cup), whereas resting tremors happen when the hands are just sitting still. Perfect nursing assessment knowledge!

question: What is a great way for a father to support the mother after childbirth?

options.A: Isolating the newborn from all family members
options.B: Taking over exclusive breastfeeding duties from the mother
options.C: Assisting with household chores to help the mother rest
options.D: Refusing to allow visitors into the family compound

explanation: New mothers need plenty of physical rest to recover, so a partner stepping in with chores is a huge help!

question: Why do some communities continue to practice FGM across generations?

options.A: Local religious texts explicitly command the surgery
options.B: Modern scientific journals endorse the procedure
options.C: It is viewed as a vital cultural rite of passage
options.D: Government health laws strongly mandate the practice

explanation: Correct! Communities hold onto FGM because it is deeply tied to their traditional customs and transition ceremonies.

question: Why should nurses use a friendly, non-judgmental tone when asking patients about drug use?

options.A: It legally protects the nurse from malpractice suits
options.B: It encourages patients to provide honest health disclosures
options.C: It ensures the doctor prescribes higher drug doses
options.D: It prevents the patient from staying in the hospital

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from moral blame, they are much more honest about their health history. Great nursing care starts with empathy!

question: Which imaging scan is usually best for getting a detailed look at the tiny pituitary gland?

options.A: Superficial ultrasound scanning
options.B: Standard chest X-ray examination
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
options.D: Radioactive iodine uptake probe

explanation: You've got this! MRI gives amazing soft-tissue pictures, making it the top choice for checking out small, deep structures like the pituitary gland.

question: What is the main purpose of the HEEADSSS tool when assessing a teenager?

options.A: To systematically screen for lifestyle risk factors and psychosocial health
options.B: To diagnose underlying genetic disorders of the endocrine system
options.C: To calculate the exact caloric requirements for daily exercise
options.D: To determine the precise biological stage of puberty

explanation: Spot on! HEEADSSS is a helpful checklist nurses use to review a teen's home life, school, mental health, and safety.

question: What is the main event that happens during ovulation?

options.A: Release of a mature egg from the ovary
options.B: Implantation of a blastocyst in the wall
options.C: Fertilization of the egg in the uterus
options.D: Shedding of the thick uterine lining

explanation: Ovulation is simply when the ovary releases a mature egg (oocyte) into the fallopian tube. You've got this!

question: How does erratic drug dosing directly affect a patient's body?

options.A: It stabilizes blood pressure within normal ranges
options.B: It helps the liver filter out toxins much faster
options.C: It ensures steady healing and faster tissue repair
options.D: It causes dangerous blood levels leading to toxicity

explanation: Unpredictable timing and dosing create wild spikes in drug concentration, pushing safe levels into toxic territory. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the specific name for Cushing's syndrome when it is caused by a tiny tumor in the pituitary gland making too much ACTH?

options.A: Cushing's disease
options.B: Conn's syndrome
options.C: Pheochromocytoma
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: Here is a handy clinical tip: 'Cushing's syndrome' is any excess cortisol, but when the pituitary gland's tumor is the culprit, we specifically call it 'Cushing's disease'.

question: What term is used specifically for the art and science of teaching adult learners?

options.A: Behaviorism
options.B: Andragogy
options.C: Pedagogy
options.D: Constructivism

explanation: Spot on! Andragogy is the special framework tailored for how adults learn best, which is quite different from how kids are taught in basic school.

question: What is the typical normal oxygen saturation range for a healthy adult breathing room air?
explanation: Healthy individuals without lung or heart disease usually maintain oxygen saturation levels between 95% and 100%. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of an endocrine suppression test?

options.A: To measure how fast the kidneys reabsorb glucose from the urine
options.B: To see if a gland stops producing hormones when given a suppressing agent
options.C: To stimulate a sleeping gland into producing maximum hormone levels
options.D: To permanently destroy overactive cells inside the adrenal cortex

explanation: Exactly! While stimulation tests wake glands up, suppression tests check if an overactive gland knows how to quiet down when it's supposed to.

question: What is one of the most common reasons nurses face malpractice claims in the ward?

options.A: Wearing incorrect uniforms
options.B: Writing incorrect patient notes
options.C: Refusing overtime shifts
options.D: Medication errors

explanation: Giving the wrong drug or incorrect dose is a leading cause of legal trouble. Always double-check your '5 Rights' of medication!

question: What was a major focus of early community health efforts during the colonial days in Nigeria?

options.A: Exporting medical equipment overseas
options.B: Providing space tourism training
options.C: Combating prevalent tropical diseases
options.D: Testing advanced robotic surgery

explanation: Early health programs had to tackle heavy burdens like malaria and smallpox that were affecting local populations.

question: How can you tell parathyroid tissue apart from thyroid tissue under a microscope?

options.A: Parathyroid glands contain large amounts of colloid material for hormone storage
options.B: Parathyroid tissue is arranged in dense cords and nests rather than hollow follicles
options.C: Parathyroid glands lack blood capillaries within their parenchymal clusters
options.D: Parathyroid tissue is lined exclusively by ciliated columnar epithelial cells

explanation: While the thyroid forms hollow ring-like 'follicles' filled with jelly, the parathyroid packs its cells into neat little clusters and cords surrounded by tiny blood vessels.

question: What is the standard first-line injection used to treat uncomplicated gonorrhea?

options.A: Ceftriaxone
options.B: Penicillin G
options.C: Metronidazole
options.D: Vancomycin

explanation: Ceftriaxone as a single injection is our go-to treatment because older drugs unfortunately don't work well anymore due to resistance.

question: What is the biggest advantage of having a separate casualty theatre in the hospital?

options.A: It completely removes the need for sterilization protocols
options.B: It reduces the number of doctors required on duty
options.C: It allows student nurses to perform surgeries independently
options.D: It preserves major operating theatres for complex and major surgeries

explanation: You nailed it! Separating minor cases from major ones ensures our heavy-duty ORs are always ready when a major surgical emergency rolls in.

question: How do blood erythropoietin levels help tell primary and secondary polycythaemia apart?

options.A: Primary has high levels, secondary has zero
options.B: Hormone levels stay normal in both conditions
options.C: Primary has low levels, secondary has high levels
options.D: Both types always show very low hormone levels

explanation: In primary, the bone marrow acts on its own, so the body stops making erythropoietin. In secondary, the body pumps out extra erythropoietin because it's begging for oxygen!

question: Why are pregnant women more prone to developing urinary tract infections?

options.A: White blood cells are absent from the body during gestation
options.B: High blood pressure forces bacteria directly into the bladder
options.C: The kidneys stop producing urine entirely for long stretches
options.D: Ureters and the renal pelvis dilate and urine flow slows down

explanation: Hormonal relaxation and physical compression cause urinary stasis in the dilated ureters, giving bacteria an easier environment to multiply. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h3)

question: A family member is feeding a stroke survivor who can actually hold a spoon with an adaptive grip. What should you do?

options.A: Recommend switching the patient entirely to liquid nutritional supplements
options.B: Praise the family member for providing thorough and efficient care
options.C: Insist that the nurse take over all feeding duties moving forward
options.D: Encourage the patient to use the adaptive spoon independently during meals

explanation: We always want to cheer patients on to do as much as they can for themselves. Independence speeds up recovery!

question: What is a key nursing duty right before a patient takes a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Confirming that the patient actually followed the fasting rules
options.B: Giving the patient a small snack to boost energy
options.C: Checking their urine output with a dipstick
options.D: Giving a quick dose of insulin just in case

explanation: Always double-check! Asking 'When was your last meal or drink?' ensures you don't send inaccurate lab samples to the path lab.

question: When is the right time to suction a patient who is on a ventilator?

options.A: Every hour on the hour strictly
options.B: Only when clinical signs indicate retained secretions
options.C: Immediately before every physician visit
options.D: Whenever the patient asks for it

explanation: Suctioning is rough on the airways and steals a bit of air. Always assess the patient first and only suction when you actually hear or see signs that they need it!

question: What is the medical term for the surgical removal of the gallbladder?

options.A: Cholecystectomy
options.B: Colectomy
options.C: Choledochotomy
options.D: Duodenostomy

explanation: You got it! A cholecystectomy is simply the surgical removal of the gallbladder, done either through tiny camera cuts or an open incision.

question: Why is keeping girls in school considered a powerful community-level defense against early marriage?

options.A: Academic settings prevent girls from ever interacting with families
options.B: Schools provide free housing for all married minors
options.C: Government laws fine parents who do not send boys to school
options.D: Education delays marriage and equips girls with economic independence skills

explanation: Education empowers girls with knowledge, raises their self-esteem, and naturally pushes the age of marriage higher. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h6)

question: Which sampling technique simply grabs participants because they are easy to reach and right in front of you?

options.A: Systematic sampling
options.B: Stratified sampling
options.C: Cluster sampling
options.D: Convenience sampling

explanation: Spot on! Convenience sampling uses whoever is readily available—like patients sitting right now in your clinic waiting room.

question: Which secondary skin lesion looks like a narrow crack going down into the skin layer?

options.A: Fissure
options.B: Ulcer
options.C: Lichenification
options.D: Excoriation

explanation: Picture chapped lips or dry, cracked heels—that's a fissure. It's a sharp, linear crack in the skin.

question: A cancer patient on chemo has a fever of 38.5°C and a very low neutrophil count. What is your immediate priority action?

options.A: Wait for routine morning blood cultures to return before calling the physician.
options.B: Administer prescribed broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics immediately.
options.C: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold citrus juices.
options.D: Apply an ice blanket to bring down the patient's core body temperature.

explanation: Safety first! Febrile neutropenia is a life-threatening emergency. Quick IV antibiotics are vital to stop rapid-fire sepsis in its tracks.

question: A patient with a history of epilepsy comes to the clinic reporting frequent seizures after spending a week studying all night for exams. Which trigger is most likely responsible?

options.A: Genetic mutation
options.B: Flashing lights
options.C: Sleep deprivation
options.D: Cerebral infection

explanation: Severe lack of rest significantly lowers the brain's seizure threshold and is a very common trigger for acute attacks. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h4)

question: During which stage of an infection does a patient feel just a bit 'off' with vague, mild symptoms, yet they easily spread the illness to others because they're still walking around?

options.A: Illness stage
options.B: Incubation period
options.C: Prodromal stage
options.D: Convalescent period

explanation: Spot on! The prodromal stage is tricky because the patient just feels mildly tired or scratchy-throated, so they keep moving about and unknowingly share germs with everyone.

question: Why do healthcare professionals use standardized anatomical terminology?

options.A: To replace traditional nursing assessment skills
options.B: To make medical records longer and more detailed
options.C: to confuse patients so they ask fewer questions
options.D: To prevent misunderstandings during clinical communication

explanation: Standardized terms give everyone a universal vocabulary so patient care details are never misunderstood across different shifts or teams. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is mild to moderate anaemia during delivery considered a serious clinical emergency?

options.A: Normal blood loss during labor can quickly push her into life-threatening shock.
options.B: It guarantees the baby will have birth defects.
options.C: It automatically stops the first stage of labor.
options.D: It stops the placenta from coming out properly.

explanation: Spotting this early is key! When a mother starts with low blood levels, even normal delivery bleeding can become dangerous very fast.

question: What is the main goal of homeostasis in the human body?

options.A: Increasing body temperature continuously
options.B: Keeping a stable internal environment
options.C: Stopping all metabolic activities
options.D: Speeding up the aging process

explanation: You've got this! Homeostasis simply means keeping your body's internal environment nice and steady, even when things change around you. Think of it as your body's built-in thermostat.

question: What is an embolus?

options.A: A traveling blood clot or foreign object moving through the bloodstream
options.B: An infection of the outer heart lining
options.C: A normal hole between the right and left atrium
options.D: A sudden widening of the aorta

explanation: An embolus is basically a traveler you don't want! It's any loose mass floating through the blood vessels until it gets stuck in a smaller vessel and blocks the path.

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the water drain off your arms?

options.A: From the elbows down toward the fingertips
options.B: Directly off the sides of the forearms
options.C: From the fingertips down toward the elbows
options.D: Upward toward the shoulders using towels

explanation: Always let water flow from your cleanest area (fingertips) down to your elbows. Gravity is your friend here!

question: You find yourself treating a patient extra nicely just because they remind you of your sweet grandmother. What is this called?

options.A: Premature termination of the therapeutic phase
options.B: A failure in active listening techniques
options.C: Cultural stereotyping of the patient's background
options.D: Boundary crossing due to countertransference

explanation: Treating a patient differently because they remind you of someone in your personal life is a classic sign of countertransference clouding your professional judgment.

question: A pregnant patient comes in with a pounding headache, changes in her vision, and very high blood pressure. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Uterine atony
options.C: Placenta previa
options.D: Preeclampsia

explanation: Well done! High blood pressure paired with headaches and visual changes are classic warning signs of preeclampsia that every nurse needs to watch out for.

question: Why do researchers often recruit more people than their minimum calculated sample size?

options.A: To increase the chance of getting statistically insignificant results
options.B: To account for participants who drop out or withdraw during the study
options.C: To satisfy hospital administrators who love large group numbers
options.D: To make the data entry process longer for student assistants

explanation: Exactly! People travel, fall ill, or change their minds. Adding a buffer upfront saves your project if participants drop out.

question: What is the main nutritional gift that cereal grains like rice, maize, and guinea corn give our bodies?

options.A: Vitamin B12 for nerve function
options.B: Complete animal protein profiles
options.C: Complex carbohydrates for energy
options.D: High amounts of dietary cholesterol

explanation: Awesome! Cereals are our main energy staples, loaded with complex carbs to keep us moving through long ward shifts and lectures.

question: You examine a child in a rural clinic and notice dry eyes and Bitot's spots. What deficiency should you suspect?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Iron
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Dry eyes and Bitot's spots are textbook signs of a Vitamin A deficiency. Great clinical catch!

question: Why are accurate meeting minutes considered important legal records in healthcare?

options.A: They serve as proof of staff attendance for annual salary increases
options.B: They provide a clear audit trail of accountability and quality improvement decisions
options.C: They act as marketing material for prospective nursing students
options.D: They replace the need for patient clinical chart documentation

explanation: Minutes show that the facility actively addressed safety and operational issues over time.

question: What is the main job of the rods in our retina?

options.A: Regulating the amount of light entering the pupil
options.B: Producing fluid for the front of the eye
options.C: Enabling sharp color vision in bright light
options.D: Functioning in dim light and detecting motion

explanation: Think of rods as your night-vision helpers! They are super sensitive to low light and movement, which helps you get around in the dark.

question: Why is cost-effectiveness a major factor when choosing essential drugs?

options.A: It guarantees that the manufacturer makes a high profit margin
options.B: It proves that the medicine was manufactured inside the country
options.C: It ensures limited financial resources can treat the maximum number of people
options.D: It eliminates the need for any healthcare workers to monitor patients

explanation: Because healthcare budgets are always restricted, choosing cost-effective options stretches funds to cover more patients in need. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using the '5 Ps' framework when taking an adolescent's health history?

options.A: To calculate the exact body mass index of the patient
options.B: To determine the nutritional requirements of the teenager
options.C: To gather a thorough and structured sexual health history
options.D: To diagnose mental health disorders like depression

explanation: Spot on! The 5 Ps (Partners, Practices, Protection, Past history, Pregnancy prevention) help nurses collect sexual health details in an organized, non-judgmental way.

question: What is the primary normal function of synovial fluid in a healthy joint?

options.A: To anchor ligaments tightly to the bone
options.B: To produce red blood cells for the joint
options.C: To reduce friction between moving bones
options.D: To send pain signals to the brain

explanation: Synovial fluid acts as a natural lubricant that protects cartilage from wear and tear during movement. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient with frequent malaria infections lives in a neighborhood with stagnant drainage water and poor housing. Which factor is most directly influencing this patient's health?

options.A: A lack of personal interest in health education
options.B: An unavoidable genetic predisposition to mosquito bites
options.C: Environmental and social determinants of health
options.D: An acute psychological response to stress

explanation: Poor living conditions and stagnant water are environmental factors that directly increase exposure to illness. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the classic sign that patients usually report when they have a bone tumor?

options.A: Itchy skin rashes directly over the affected joint
options.B: Sudden numbness and tingling in the toes of both feet
options.C: Persistent, worsening bone pain that is often present at night
options.D: Sharp shooting pain that only happens during heavy physical exercise

explanation: Unlike normal muscle aches, bone tumor pain is relentless, gets worse over time, and loves to wake patients up at night.

question: How should you take a Plaster of Paris bandage roll out of the basin of water?

options.A: Shake the roll vigorously in the air until the water stops dripping
options.B: Leave the roll soaking in the water until ready for the next layer
options.C: Gently squeeze both ends to remove excess water without twisting
options.D: Wring the roll tightly like a wet towel to make it completely dry

explanation: Never twist the roll because it messes up the plaster structure! A gentle squeeze from the ends gets rid of extra water safely.

question: Which group of hospitalized individuals faces the highest risk for severe falls?

options.A: Older adult patients
options.B: Visiting family members
options.C: Young pediatric infants
options.D: Night shift desk nurses

explanation: Aging bodies often experience muscle weakness, balance issues, and dizziness from medications, making older adults much more vulnerable to falls. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which part of the Glasgow Coma Scale is usually seen as the best clue to how well a patient will recover?

options.A: Verbal response
options.B: Pupillary reflex
options.C: Motor response
options.D: Eye opening

explanation: The motor response checks deep brain pathways. It gives nurses and doctors the strongest clue about how a patient is recovering after a head injury.

question: Roughly what percentage of an adult human body is made up of water?

options.A: 30 percent
options.B: 10 percent
options.C: 95 percent
options.D: 60 percent

explanation: Water makes up about 60% of an adult's weight! It's the essential fluid environment where all our body's chemical reactions happen.

question: Why should you never use both hands to recap a used needle?

options.A: It bends the needle tip and makes the injection painful
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of an accidental needle-stick injury
options.C: It violates hospital policies regarding medication waste disposal
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy medication round

explanation: Using two hands to recap makes it way too easy to miss the cap and puncture your own finger. Safety first—keep that hand away from the sharp end!

question: When handling a wet plaster cast, why should nurses use the palms of their hands instead of their fingertips?

options.A: To stop the wet plaster material from sticking permanently to skin
options.B: To prevent indentations that can cause pressure sores on the skin
options.C: To prevent the nurse from getting skin irritation from chemicals
options.D: To make sure the heavy cast does not crack before it dries

explanation: Fingertips leave deep dents in wet plaster. Those little flat spots can press painfully against the skin and cause pressure ulcers later.

question: Why is building trust with the community so important for a nurse?

options.A: It legally protects the nurse from medical malpractice lawsuits
options.B: It encourages community members to accept immunizations and report illnesses early
options.C: It eliminates the need for any environmental sanitation work
options.D: It guarantees financial funding from international donors

explanation: Spot on! People are much more likely to listen, take their vaccines, and share health worries when they know and trust their nurse.

question: What is the primary medical treatment for endocrine hyposecretion?

options.A: High-dose antibiotic therapy
options.B: Hormone replacement therapy
options.C: Strict long-term fluid restriction
options.D: Surgical removal of the gland

explanation: Simple logic: if the body isn't making enough of a vital hormone, we replace it with medication!

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Using private rooms
options.C: Taking daily antibiotics
options.D: Proper hand hygiene

explanation: Spot on! Simple, regular handwashing is the absolute number one tool we have to keep germs from jumping from patient to patient.

question: Which baby outcome is most common in pregnancies among very young adolescents?

options.A: Childhood developmental hyperactive disorders
options.B: Macrosomia and post-term delivery
options.C: Low birth weight and prematurity
options.D: Congenital bone malformations

explanation: Because the young mother's body is still developing and sharing nutrients, babies are often born early and weigh less than normal.

question: Why should you avoid tilting an infant's head too far back when opening their airway?

options.A: It completely stops spontaneous breathing
options.B: It always causes immediate cervical spine fractures
options.C: The flexible trachea can kink and cause an obstruction
options.D: It makes it impossible to check the pulse

explanation: An infant's windpipe is soft and flexible. If you tilt their head back too far (hyperextension), the airway actually kinks shut like a bent garden hose!

question: Why do pre-existing medical conditions often get worse during pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy significantly increases the workload on the mother's heart, lungs, and kidneys
options.B: Metabolic rates drop drastically to conserve energy for the developing baby
options.C: Hormonal surges permanently deactivate prescribed medications in the bloodstream
options.D: The growing fetus directly consumes all of the mother's circulating red blood cells

explanation: The body experiences a massive increase in blood volume and cardiac output to support the baby, which puts extra stress on organs that were already struggling. You're mastering maternal physiology!

question: An HIV-positive mum asks if she can give her two-month-old baby sips of plain water during hot weather. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Suggest replacing one daily breastfeed with clean water to test tolerance
options.B: Encourage small amounts of boiled water to prevent dehydration in the heat
options.C: Advise against water because it can damage the gut lining and increase HIV transmission risk
options.D: Approve the water provided it is boiled and cooled beforehand

explanation: Even simple water can disrupt a baby's delicate tummy lining, making it easier for the virus to pass through. Stick to exclusive breastfeeding!

question: What is an easy, key nursing action to help prevent pneumonia in patients on a breathing machine (ventilator)?

options.A: Changing the endotracheal tube every twelve hours
options.B: Administering intravenous antibiotics to all ventilated patients
options.C: Keeping the room temperature below twenty degrees Celsius
options.D: Elevating the head of the bed between 30 and 45 degrees

explanation: Raising the bed head keeps oral and stomach secretions from sliding down into the lungs. Simple position changes make a massive difference!

question: A patient gets an allergic rash after taking a small antibiotic pill that binds to their blood proteins. What do we call this type of drug molecule?

options.A: T-independent antigen
options.B: Hapten
options.C: Superantigen
options.D: Autoantigen

explanation: Spot on! The small drug acts as a hapten, attaching to bigger body proteins and tricking the immune system into an allergic reaction.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical long-term complication of untreated polycythaemia vera?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia from suppressed bone marrow
options.B: Progression into acute leukemia
options.C: Transformation into myelofibrosis
options.D: Arterial and venous blood clots

explanation: Polycythaemia is all about having *too many* red blood cells, not iron deficiency anemia. Clots and bone marrow changes are the real long-term risks to watch out for.

question: When programming an electronic IV infusion pump on the ward, what unit of measurement do you normally use?

options.A: Milliliters per hour (mL/hr)
options.B: Liters per 24 hours (L/day)
options.C: Drops per minute (gtt/min)
options.D: Drops per second (gtt/sec)

explanation: Spot on! Pumps are designed to deliver a precise volume of fluid every hour, so we program them in mL/hr.

question: Why must used needles and razor blades go straight into a puncture-proof sharps box?

options.A: To comply with waste disposal rules without needing to wash them first
options.B: To ensure that they can be easily sharpened and reused for the next patient
options.C: To keep the delivery tray looking neat and tidy during the procedure
options.D: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries and bloodborne pathogen transmission

explanation: Sharps safety keeps everyone safe! Dropping them right in the box protects you, your colleagues, and waste handlers from nasty infections like HIV or hepatitis.

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of giving a daily bed bath to a very ill patient?

options.A: Providing gentle touch and comfort to the patient
options.B: Permanently curing chronic underlying heart disease
options.C: Removing sweat and bacteria from the skin surface
options.D: Allowing the nurse to inspect the skin for early redness

explanation: Bed baths are amazing for hygiene, comfort, and skin checks, but they unfortunately can't fix chronic internal conditions like heart disease.

question: What is the standard first-line oral antibiotic for treating non-severe pneumonia in under-fives?

options.A: Amoxicillin
options.B: Ciprofloxacin
options.C: Vancomycin
options.D: Tetracycline

explanation: Amoxicillin is the go-to first-line oral treatment for uncomplicated pneumonia because it safely and effectively fights common chest infections.

question: Why do nurses often mix pain meds with comfort measures like positioning and gentle massage?

options.A: Hospital policies strictly forbid using only drugs for post-operative patients
options.B: Non-pharmacological methods can completely replace the need for prescription painkillers
options.C: Medications work much slower if physical comfort measures are skipped
options.D: It targets pain through multiple pathways and reduces reliance on heavy medication doses

explanation: Combining approaches attacks pain from different angles. It helps patients feel better faster while keeping drug side effects as low as possible.

question: Why should loose throw rugs be removed from a patient's home after surgery?

options.A: They easily slide underfoot and cause dangerous falls.
options.B: They prevent the wheelchair wheels from rolling smoothly.
options.C: They trap moisture and cause the home humidity to rise.
options.D: They block the medical equipment from plugging into the wall.

explanation: Unsecured rugs love to slip on smooth floors, making them a major tripping hazard for anyone learning to get around with new supports.

question: Which of the following describes an independent double-check for high-risk medication calculations?

options.A: The doctor and patient calculate the pill count together at discharge
options.B: The pharmacist calculates the dose and the nurse administers it without review
options.C: One nurse calculates the dose twice on two different patient charts
options.D: Two nurses calculate the dose separately without discussing their numbers beforehand

explanation: Independent double-checks require two clinicians to work out the math separately to catch hidden errors before administration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h9)

question: Why is an oxytocic medicine a must-have in your home delivery bag?

options.A: To actively manage the third stage of labor and prevent bleeding
options.B: To help dilate the cervix more quickly in early labor
options.C: To relieve severe labor pain during the second stage
options.D: To stimulate milk production before the baby is born

explanation: You got it! Oxytocin makes the uterus clamp down strongly after delivery, which is our absolute best defense against heavy postpartum bleeding.

question: In the chain of infection, what is considered the final link?

options.A: The portal of exit
options.B: The reservoir of infection
options.C: The susceptible host
options.D: The infectious agent

explanation: You've got this! The chain ends with the susceptible host—that's a person who doesn't have enough immunity to fight off the germ.

question: Which deficiency disease is caused by a serious lack of Vitamin C?

options.A: Beriberi
options.B: Rickets
options.C: Scurvy
options.D: Pellagra

explanation: You got it! Without enough Vitamin C, your body can't make collagen properly, leading to scurvy (bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds).

question: Which component must be identical in both generic and brand name drugs?

options.A: The retail price in the pharmacy
options.B: The proprietary marketing title
options.C: The active pharmaceutical ingredient
options.D: The inactive coloring dyes

explanation: Regulatory bodies ensure that whether you buy the expensive brand name or the affordable generic, the active healing ingredient inside is 100% the same.

question: A young adult is admitted after taking too many sleeping pills on purpose. They are now fully awake and stable. What is your most important immediate nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for vitamins.
options.B: Initiate strict suicide precautions and ensure constant observation.
options.C: Scold the patient regarding the dangers of taking medication.
options.D: Restrict all family members from visiting to maintain hospital quiet.

explanation: Just because they look physically stable doesn't mean the emotional crisis is over. Safety first—keep them under close watch and arrange mental health support right away.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common risk factor for developing osteomyelitis?

options.A: Recent bone surgery
options.B: Diabetes mellitus
options.C: Intravenous drug use
options.D: Regular aerobic exercise

explanation: Regular physical activity strengthens the body and is not a risk factor for bone infections, unlike diabetes, drug use, and surgery. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of medical care for a patient diagnosed with CJD?

options.A: Relieving symptoms and providing comfort
options.B: Stopping the replication of prions
options.C: Restoring lost memory and brain cells
options.D: Reversing the genetic mutation

explanation: Correct! Because there is currently no cure for CJD, treatment is all about palliative care—keeping the patient comfortable and easing their symptoms.

question: Which body organ is mainly responsible for breaking down most oral cough medications?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Liver
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Kidneys

explanation: The liver is our chemical processing plant—it breaks down oral drugs using special enzymes before the body clears them.

question: How far should an adult rectal suppository be inserted past the anal sphincter by the nurse?

options.A: All the way into the ascending colon
options.B: Just inside the outer skin folds
options.C: 2.5 to 5 centimeters
options.D: 10 to 12 centimeters

explanation: Inserting it 2.5 to 5 cm past the internal sphincter ensures the medication stays in place and does not slip right back out. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h7)

question: What is a major long-term risk for a woman who has had repeated bouts of salpingitis?

options.A: Chronic swelling of the lower legs
options.B: Development of uterine fibroids
options.C: Permanent cessation of menstruation
options.D: Infertility and ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Scars from repeated infections can block the tubes, making it harder to get pregnant or increasing the risk of an ectopic pregnancy.

question: Which sign tells you an elderly patient with severe diarrhoea is slipping into advanced dehydration?

options.A: Slow, deep breathing with warm, flushed skin
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and delayed capillary refill
options.C: High blood pressure and excessive saliva production
options.D: Increased muscle strength in the lower limbs

explanation: A dry mouth, sticky tongue, and sluggish refill when you press the fingernail mean there just isn't enough fluid circulating in the body anymore.

question: What is the primary reason for initiating a patient referral to another facility?

options.A: The hospital building needs routine plumbing repairs
options.B: The patient's clinical needs exceed current facility resources
options.C: The attending doctor wants to take a short vacation
options.D: The patient complains about the food quality on the ward

explanation: Referrals are done when specialized care, advanced equipment, or specific expertise is required that the current health center cannot provide. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core pillar emphasized in the Astana Declaration for modern PHC?

options.A: Building exclusive luxury medical resorts for international medical tourists
options.B: Working across multiple sectors like education and environment
options.C: Empowering individuals and communities to take charge of their health
options.D: Securing strong political commitment and sustained public investment

explanation: Luxury medical tourism for the elite is not part of the Astana pillars, which focus on grassroots universal health coverage for all. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a major problem when clinics are not youth-friendly?

options.A: High rates of untreated sexually transmitted infections among teens
options.B: Mandatory health insurance for all teenagers
options.C: Decreased interest in secondary school education
options.D: An immediate surplus of qualified midwives

explanation: If young people feel judged or scared when visiting a clinic, they simply stay away. This means infections and health issues go untreated. Making our clinics welcoming changes everything!

question: A nurse researcher wants to compare the average blood pressure of patients across four different clinics at the same time. Which test is best?

options.A: Independent t-test
options.B: Paired t-test
options.C: Null hypothesis test
options.D: ANOVA

explanation: That's right! Whenever you are comparing averages across three or more groups at once, ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) is the test you need.

question: Why does the midpiece of a spermatozoon contain a large concentration of mitochondria?

options.A: To protect the genetic material from chemical damage
options.B: To manufacture extra testosterone during transit
options.C: To help the sperm attach securely to the egg wall
options.D: To produce enough energy for the tail to swim

explanation: Mitochondria act as cellular powerhouses, generating the ATP energy necessary for the flagellum to propel the sperm. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h6)

question: What does 'asepsis' mean in your daily nursing practice?

options.A: The complete destruction of all life forms on human skin
options.B: The chemical disinfection of hospital floors and walls
options.C: The total absence of disease-producing microorganisms
options.D: The administration of prophylactic antibiotics before surgery

explanation: Great job! Asepsis simply means keeping an environment or item free from harmful germs that cause infections. You've got this!

question: A child keeps coming back to the clinic with severe diarrhea. What should you check first?

options.A: Assessing the family's source of drinking water and home sanitation
options.B: Telling the mother to stop feeding the child local home-cooked meals
options.C: Prescribing stronger antibiotics and keeping the child in the ward
options.D: Advising the parents to move to a different country entirely

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! Repeated diarrhea usually points to dirty water or poor home hygiene, so checking the root cause stops the cycle.

question: Why do we treat broken glass ampoules with the same care as needles?

options.A: They dissolve quickly inside standard trash bins
options.B: They are made from recycled hospital plastics
options.C: They contain live viral vaccines inside them
options.D: They can easily puncture skin and cause deep cuts

explanation: Any broken glass with a sharp edge can cut you and introduce nasty germs. Treat them like needles!

question: How does estrogen impact a growing teenager's height during puberty?

options.A: It only lengthens the bones of the arms and legs without stopping
options.B: It permanently prevents any linear height growth from occurring
options.C: It has no effect on skeletal development or bone length
options.D: It accelerates bone growth but also causes early closure of growth plates

explanation: You nailed it! Estrogen gives teens a fast growth spurt at first, but it also signals the growth plates to eventually fuse and close up.

question: How do PET and SPECT scans differ from standard CT or MRI scans?

options.A: They measure metabolic activity and blood flow instead of just structure
options.B: They are completely non-invasive and never use injections
options.C: They take less than 30 seconds to finish
options.D: They rely purely on sound waves

explanation: While CT and MRI show what things look like, PET and SPECT show how the brain's cells are actually working.

question: Why is it important for nurses to review immunization registers regularly?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff salary and allowances
options.B: To identify children who have missed scheduled doses and need tracking
options.C: To find out which vaccine brand is most expensive
options.D: To report families to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Regular register checks help nurses spot missing children early so they can organize follow-up visits before outbreaks happen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: What is the main difference between nutritional screening and a full nutritional assessment?

options.A: Screening is done by doctors, while assessment is done by cooks
options.B: Screening is only used for children, while assessment is for adults
options.C: Screening is a quick check to find risk, while assessment is a deep dive
options.D: Screening only looks at lab work, while assessment only looks at weight

explanation: Screening quickly identifies who is at risk, prompting a thorough assessment to diagnose specific nutritional problems. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h4)

question: What visual sign immediately confirms a successful intradermal PPD injection?

options.A: A flat red rash spreading on the arm
options.B: A small droplet of bright red blood
options.C: Immediate bruising around the needle
options.D: A pale raised skin bleb or wheal

explanation: A proper intradermal injection creates a distinct bump or wheal on the skin surface, showing the fluid is trapped in the correct layer. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h4)

question: How does permethrin cream work against skin bugs like scabies mites and lice?

options.A: By blocking their ability to absorb oxygen through the skin
options.B: By dissolving the outer exoskeleton through extreme acidity
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to attack the eggs
options.D: By disrupting sodium channels and causing paralysis

explanation: Permethrin messes up the nerve signals in the bug's sodium channels, freezing their muscles so they become paralyzed and die.

question: Which body parts are included in the appendicular region?

options.A: Thorax and abdomen
options.B: Spine and pelvis
options.C: Upper and lower limbs
options.D: Head and neck

explanation: The appendicular region contains all the bones and soft tissues of the upper and lower extremities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the most crucial nursing check right after a neck biopsy or fine-needle aspiration?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of airway obstruction or bleeding
options.B: Checking for sudden spikes in fasting blood glucose
options.C: Testing the patient's 24-hour urine catecholamine levels
options.D: Encouraging immediate heavy physical exercise

explanation: Always protect the airway! Since the procedure is right in the neck near major blood vessels and the trachea, nurses must watch closely for swelling or bleeding.

question: Why is patient confidentiality especially important for an occupational health nurse?

options.A: It encourages workers to seek help for personal or health issues without fear of job loss
options.B: It stops employees from talking to each other during working hours
options.C: It allows the company to hide safety violations from the public
options.D: It prevents government regulatory bodies from inspecting the workplace

explanation: Trust is everything! When workers know their medical secrets are safe with you, they will freely report symptoms and get help early. Brilliant work today!

question: What is the correct immediate nursing action when a patient says they feel dizzy and are about to faint?

options.A: Tell the patient to stand up straight and take deep breaths.
options.B: Help the patient safely lie down on the floor.
options.C: Walk the patient quickly to the nearest chair.
options.D: Offer the patient a hot cup of coffee immediately.

explanation: Lying down prevents a dangerous fall and helps restore blood flow to the brain before blacking out completely. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h6)

question: Why does the choice of the muscle site affect how fast a drug works?

options.A: Thicker muscles destroy the active drug ingredients
options.B: Some muscle fibers actively push the medicine out
options.C: Certain sites completely block liquid absorption
options.D: Different muscles have different levels of blood supply

explanation: Blood flow drives absorption speed, so a site with poor circulation will slow down how fast the drug enters the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h1)

question: If an endotracheal tube advances too far down the trachea, which mainstem bronchus does it most commonly enter?

options.A: The right mainstem bronchus
options.B: It enters both mainstems equally
options.C: It stops directly at the carina
options.D: The left mainstem bronchus

explanation: The right main bronchus has a wider and more vertical angle, making it much easier for a deep tube to slip into it by mistake. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h7)

question: What role do humans play in the life cycle of Taenia tapeworms when they harbor the adult worm in their intestines?

options.A: Dead-end host
options.B: Accidental host
options.C: Definitive host
options.D: Intermediate host

explanation: Spot on! Because humans house the adult tapeworm in the gut, we are considered the definitive host. Keep up the great practice!

question: What is the most helpful advice a nurse can give to a patient who frequently chokes on their food?

options.A: Take a strong sleeping pill before meals to relax
options.B: Cut food into small pieces and avoid talking while chewing
options.C: Drink a large glass of cold water with every bite
options.D: Lie flat on your back right after finishing your meal

explanation: Simple habits make a big difference. Taking small bites, chewing thoroughly, and focusing on your food instead of chatting helps prevent accidental choking.

question: A patient is rushed in unconscious, with very tiny pupils (pinpoint) and slow, shallow breathing. What type of poison do you suspect?

options.A: Stimulants
options.B: Anticholinergics
options.C: Opioids
options.D: Household bleach

explanation: You nailed it! Pinpoint pupils combined with depressed breathing are the classic textbook signs of an opioid overdose.

question: What is the main reason nurses ask patients to take off all jewelry and hairpins before an MRI?

options.A: To keep the changing rooms clean and organized
options.B: To prevent static electricity from building up on clothing
options.C: To stop the patient from losing valuables during the test
options.D: To prevent metal objects from turning into dangerous projectiles

explanation: Spot on! That giant magnet can pull loose metal items like a flying bullet, which could hurt someone or break the machine.

question: During the teenage growth spurt, which part of the body experiences a massive doubling in mass?

options.A: Skeletal mass
options.B: Neural tissue
options.C: Lymphoid tissue
options.D: Adipose tissue

explanation: Spot on! Bone growth speeds up like crazy during puberty, causing a teen's skeletal mass to roughly double. You've got this!

question: What is the best home-care advice for a patient's small wound sites after laparoscopy?

options.A: Scrub the incisions vigorously with a rough sponge
options.B: Apply heavy grease daily to speed up healing
options.C: Keep the puncture sites clean and dry
options.D: Remove the surgical steri-strips immediately

explanation: Correct! Keeping tiny cut sites clean and dry keeps germs away and lets them heal nicely without any trouble.

question: Why does the outer layer of the skin (epidermis) have to rely on diffusion to get its nutrients?

options.A: It is made entirely of dead cells.
options.B: It repels blood vessels using keratin.
options.C: It is too thick for capillaries to enter.
options.D: It lacks a direct blood supply.

explanation: Exactly! The epidermis doesn't have its own blood vessels (it's avascular). Because of this, nutrients have to quietly seep up from the dermis living right below it.

question: Why does injured skin become extra sensitive (hyperalgesia) after a burn?

options.A: Blood flow increases to the area to speed up nerve regeneration.
options.B: Injured tissue becomes more sensitive to protect it from further harm.
options.C: Nerve endings permanently shut down to prevent shock.
options.D: The brain completely blocks out pain signals from surrounding skin.

explanation: Spot on! This extra sensitivity lowers your pain threshold on purpose, making you protect the healing area while it recovers.

question: How does nurse involvement in community support networks benefit the broader health system?

options.A: It empowers volunteers and lightens the workload on formal clinic staff
options.B: It restricts patient interactions strictly inside the hospital building
options.C: It ensures that nurses make all decisions without community input
options.D: It eliminates the need for any medications in chronic disease care

explanation: By training community members to help run support networks, health centers extend their reach and ease pressure on busy clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h6)
